guide.title: What is a Skill?
guide.lead: A Skill is a written guide that tells Claude how to do a certain kind of work. Install it once and Claude pulls it up whenever your request matches.
guide.why1: You stop re-explaining the same thing every time.
guide.why2: Fiddly work like slide decks, spreadsheets and document cleanup gets done a consistent way.
guide.why3: Skills load only when relevant, so many installed Skills don't slow Claude down.
guide.howApp: Claude desktop/web users: download the ZIP on a skill page and upload it in Claude's settings. No terminal.
guide.howCode: Claude Code users: copy the sentence on the skill page and paste it to Claude — it installs the skill for you.
guide.safeBody: Skills carry instructions and runnable code. For unfamiliar repositories, read the source first. This site points to public GitHub repositories and does not vouch for skill contents.

onramp.title: What you can do right now, without a skill
onramp.lead: These are just phrasings you paste into Claude. They aren't built-in commands, so you retype them every time. Installing a skill makes this happen on its own.
onramp.s1: Summarize this in three lines, key points only
onramp.s2: Tell me honestly where this code is weak
onramp.s3: Rewrite this interface copy so it reads naturally
onramp.s4: Give me five opening lines that make people keep reading
onramp.s5: This sentence reads awkwardly. Rewrite it
onramp.s6: Put these options in a comparison table by criteria
onramp.s7: Turn this task into a checklist with nothing missed
onramp.s8: Explain it very simply, like to a ten-year-old

terminal.title: The very easy guide to the Claude Code terminal
terminal.lead: That black window looks scary, right? It's really just where you ask your computer for things in writing. Follow the steps below and you'll be done in ten minutes. Both Windows and Mac are covered.
terminal.whatBody: Normally you click an icon to open a program. A terminal is a window where you say it in writing instead. Type one line like "install this for me" and the computer does it. Nothing scary — just a different way of talking.
terminal.needPlan: You need a paid Claude plan — Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise. The free plan does not include Claude Code.
terminal.needOs: macOS 13 or newer, or Windows 10 or newer. Almost any recent computer works.
terminal.needNode: Nothing else to install. Node.js used to be required; it isn't anymore.
terminal.macOpen: Press ⌘ (Command) + Space together. A search box appears in the middle of the screen. Type `terminal` and press Enter — the black window opens.
terminal.winOpen: Click the Start button (the window shape) at the bottom left and type `powershell`. Click Windows PowerShell at the top and the blue window opens.
terminal.winNote: You don't need to run it as Administrator. A normal click is fine.
terminal.installBody: Paste the line below into the window you just opened and press Enter. Use the copy button rather than typing it yourself.
terminal.installWait: Text will stream past. Wait one or two minutes and it's done. Don't close the window while it runs.
terminal.checkBody: Type this and press Enter. If you see a number like `2.1.211 (Claude Code)`, you're done.
terminal.checkFail: Seeing `command not found` or "not recognized"? Close the window and open a new one, then try again. That fixes it most of the time.
terminal.loginBody: Type just `claude` and press Enter — a browser window opens by itself. Pick your Claude account, approve it, and you're in. You only do this once.
terminal.folderTitle: 7. Start inside the folder you want to work in
terminal.folderBody: Claude Code reads the files in "the folder you're currently in", so move into your project folder first.
terminal.folderMac: Mac tip: type `cd ` (with one space) and then drag the folder onto the terminal window — the path fills itself in. Press Enter, then type `claude`.
terminal.folderWin: Windows tip: open the folder, click the address bar at the top to copy the path, then paste it after `cd `.
terminal.skillBody: That's the setup done. Pick a skill on Claude Skill Mart, copy its "Let Claude do it" line, and paste it into the `claude` session you just started — it installs the skill for you.
terminal.stuck1: Typed a command and nothing happened → check that you pressed Enter.
terminal.stuck2: `command not found` → close the window, open a new one, and try again.
terminal.stuck3: The sign-in window doesn't open → open a browser first, then type `claude` again.
terminal.stuck4: A message about your plan → the free plan won't work; you need Pro or above.
terminal.stuckAsk: Still stuck? Message the developer below. A screenshot of where it stopped makes it much faster.
